주제찾기
1 1번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
The Venus flytrap is a carnivorous plant whose paired leaves work as both mouth and stomach. Tiny hairs stand on the inner face of each leaf, waiting for something to brush against them. A single touch, however, is not enough to shut the leaf. Laboratory tests revealed that the plant keeps track of how often those hairs are bumped. It also measures the gap between one bump and the next, closing only when two arrive inside twenty seconds. Should that window expire, the plant simply starts its count over from zero. More than three touches are needed before digestive chemicals are released. Because of this careful arithmetic, rain and falling leaves never fool the plant into wasting energy.
①how a carnivorous plant uses counting to tell real prey from false alarms
②why insects are attracted to the bright inner surface of flytrap leaves
③the chemical structure of the enzymes that break down animal tissue
④how gardeners can grow Venus flytraps successfully at home
⑤the evolutionary reason plants gave up photosynthesis for hunting
2 2번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Engineers use the term negative pressure for a sealed space whose pressure sits below that of everything around it. Break the wall between two such spaces, and matter always rushes from the higher side toward the lower one. Undersea oil lines are deliberately kept in this low-pressure condition. If such a line cracks, seawater pours inward instead of oil spilling outward. That inward flow is far kinder to the ocean than a leak would be. City drinking-water mains, however, show the same principle turning dangerous. A damaged main can draw polluted groundwater straight into the public supply. For that reason gauges and valves are installed to watch and adjust the pressure inside.
①the reasons why groundwater near cities becomes contaminated
②the history of measuring instruments such as gauges and valves
③the difficulty of repairing pipes once seawater has entered them
④the engineering methods used to build pipelines on the ocean floor
⑤the same pressure principle that protects oil pipelines can endanger water pipes

주제찾기
3 3번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Once in every four years February is handed a twenty-ninth day. That extra square on the calendar is called Leap Day. Its purpose is to keep the months we count and the seasons we live through pointing at the same thing. A year feels like a tidy 365 days, yet the true circuit of Earth around the sun takes about 365.2421 days. The leftover quarter of a day has to be repaid, and four years of it make one whole day. Skip that repayment and winter would slide earlier and earlier through the calendar year. Farmers planting by the calendar would meet frost too soon, and harvests would fail. Festivals tied to a season or a date would drift away from the moment they were meant to mark.
①why an extra day must be added to keep the calendar matched to the seasons
②how ancient astronomers first measured the length of a solar year
③the customs that different countries observe on the twenty-ninth of February
④the reason February is shorter than every other month of the year
⑤how crop failures have shaped the history of farming communities
4 4번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
In 2011 an elderly Brazilian named Joao Pereira de Souza was walking the beach of his island village near Rio de Janeiro. There he came upon a penguin too weak to stand, its feathers heavy with oil. He took the starving bird home, cleaned it, fed it, and called it Dindim. When it was strong again he carried it back to the water and said goodbye for good. The farewell did not last, because Dindim came back. Experts believe the bird covers roughly 5,000 miles between the old man's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. It repeats that journey every single year without fail. After about eight months at the village it leaves to breed, and then it returns once more.
①the growing popularity of island villages near Rio de Janeiro
②a rescued penguin's yearly return to the man who saved its life
③the damage that oil spills cause to seabirds along the Brazilian coast
④the migration routes that penguins follow between Argentina and Chile
⑤the difficulty of raising wild animals inside a human household

요지찾기
5 1번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Meat-eating plants must decide when something touching them is worth catching. The Venus flytrap solves this problem with a pair of leaves that serve as jaws and a stomach. Trigger hairs line the inner surface, and brushing them once does nothing at all. An experiment showed that the plant registers the number of touches it receives. It even times them, snapping shut only when two touches fall within a twenty second window. After twenty seconds have gone by, the counter returns to zero. Enzymes appear only after the count passes three, confirming that live prey is inside. This arithmetic keeps the plant from spending its energy on raindrops or fallen leaves.
①육식 식물은 곤충보다 빗물에서 더 많은 양분을 얻는다.
②파리지옥풀은 자극의 횟수와 간격을 세어 헛된 소비를 피한다.
③식물의 감각모는 동물의 신경 세포와 구조가 동일하다.
④파리지옥풀의 잎은 한 번 닫히면 다시 열리지 않는다.
⑤덫 식물은 다른 식물보다 훨씬 빠르게 성장한다.
6 2번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Negative pressure describes a closed space held at a pressure lower than its surroundings. Whenever the barrier between two spaces fails, material moves from high pressure to low. Oil pipes on the sea floor take advantage of this rule. Because they are kept below the surrounding pressure, a crack lets ocean water in rather than oil out. The sea is spared the spill that would otherwise follow. The very same rule works against municipal water pipes. Damage there can pull contaminated groundwater into the drinking supply. So the pressure in those lines must be measured and controlled with care.
①압력 차이가 없는 배관 설계가 가장 안전한 방식이다.
②계량기와 밸브는 배관의 파손 자체를 막아 주는 장치이다.
③해저 송유관은 상수도관보다 훨씬 튼튼하게 만들어야 한다.
④지하수는 언제나 바닷물보다 더 심각하게 오염되어 있다.
⑤음압은 쓰이는 곳에 따라 이롭기도 해롭기도 하므로 세심한 관리가 필요하다.

7 3번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Every fourth February receives one additional day, known as Leap Day. It exists so that our calendar and the seasons never fall out of step. We treat a year as 365 days, but Earth actually needs about 365.2421 days to circle the sun. Those extra hours pile up, and every four years they amount to a full day that must be added back. Without that correction, winter would arrive earlier and earlier on the calendar. Agricultural schedules built around dates would fail, and crops could be lost. Holidays and cultural celebrations are also tied to particular seasons or dates. Left uncorrected, those events would slowly wander away from the times they were meant to honor.

9 1번 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Among plants that feed on flesh, the Venus flytrap stands out for its patience. Its two facing leaves close like jaws and then digest what they hold. Fine hairs on the inner surface report every touch to the plant. Yet one report is ignored, because a single touch may mean nothing at all. Researchers found that the trap shuts only after two touches within twenty seconds. If the second touch comes too late, the whole process resets. Only when the touches exceed three does the plant start making digestive enzymes. Thanks to that rule, no raindrop or fallen leaf ever costs the plant a meal's worth of energy.
①How Insects Escape from Hungry Leaves
②The Fastest Growing Plants on Earth
③A Plant That Counts Before It Closes

10 2번 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Pressure inside a sealed space can be set lower than the pressure outside it. Engineers call this state negative pressure, and it decides which way things move. When a barrier breaks, substances always travel toward the low-pressure side. Pipes carrying oil beneath the sea are held in that state on purpose. A break in them fills the pipe with seawater instead of releasing oil into the water. Municipal drinking-water lines, however, reveal the other face of the same rule. If they are damaged, they may suck contaminated groundwater into the supply. Gauges and valves therefore keep constant watch over the pressure inside them.
①The Double Life of Negative Pressure
②Cleaning Up Oil Spills on the Ocean Floor
③How Cities Find Fresh Groundwater Underground

A damaged main does not leak outward; it swallows whatever lies in the soil around it. The lesson is that negative pressure is . What matters is what surrounds the pipe and what the pipe is carrying. That is why gauges and valves must adjust the pressure line by line.

The Venus flytrap, a meat-eating plant, has a pair of leaves that act as jaws and a stomach. If an insect touches the trigger hairs on the surface of these leaves, the leaves close, trapping the insect. Amazingly, a recent experiment showed that the Venus flytrap knew how many times its trigger hairs were touched and could even count the time between these stimuli. The trap closed only if the plant sensed two stimuli within a 20 second time span. Once 20 seconds passed, the process was reset. In addition, more than three stimuli were required for the plant to begin producing the enzymes that digest the trapped insect. Thanks to this process, the Venus flytrap doesn't make meaningful efforts trying to trap and digest raindrops or fallen leaves.

"Negative pressure" refers to a situation in which the pressure of an enclosed area is lower than that of the surrounding area. If the barrier between these two areas breaks, any substances in the high-pressure area will immediately flow into the low-pressure area. For example, undersea pipes used to transport oil are in a state of negative pressure; therefore, any break in the pipeline will cause it to fill with ocean water. This is much better than the opposite scenario, in which oil would be released into the ocean. However, negative pressure is not always beneficial, such as in the case of pipes carrying drinking water to a city. If these municipal waterlines are damaged, they can potentially suck in contaminated groundwater, which would then enter the water supply. For this reason, a system of gauges and valves is used to adjust and control their pressure.

While we think that a normal year consists of 365 days, it actually takes Earth about 365.2421 days to orbit the sun. Every four years, it is necessary to add an extra day to account for the lost time. Without the addition of a leap day, winter would occur earlier in the calendar year, causing problems for agricultural schedules and potentially leading to crop failures. Additionally, many holidays and cultural celebrations are linked to specific seasons or dates. Without leap years to keep the calendar in check, these events would gradually drift away from their intended time of celebration.
